name: fluid-synth
desc: Real-time software synthesizer based on the SoundFont 2 specs
why: A real-time SoundFont synthesizer that can be driven from MIDI or the terminal, a good instrument to poke at, though fairly well known.

brief.what_it_is: FluidSynth is a real-time software synthesizer based on the SoundFont 2 specification. It generates audio from MIDI events, read from MIDI input devices, using a SoundFont as its instrument bank, so it works as the software equivalent of a hardware MIDI synth. It can also play MIDI files. It has no graphical interface of its own. It ships a built-in command line shell and a shared library that other programs can embed.
brief.why_it_exists: The author's framing is that FluidSynth came out of an online multi-user game project that wanted SoundFont-based music: wavetable synthesis is cheap on CPU, and small MIDI files plus SoundFonts are easier to download than audio. Since sound had to work on Linux, macOS and Windows with any sound card, the team needed a software SoundFont synthesizer.
brief.how_it_works: The README says it reads and handles MIDI events from MIDI input devices and renders them to audio using a SoundFont. Its design goal was to stay self-contained, with no platform-specific libraries and no external dependencies, so it could be embedded as a plugin, loaded dynamically, or wrapped in language bindings and game frameworks. The homepage adds real-time effect control through SoundFont 2.04 modulators and support for SoundFont 3 (Vorbis-compressed SF2), DLS Level 1 and 2, and playback of MIDI files.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the README points to the wiki page BuildingWithCMake for building from source, which implies CMake. I did not open the wiki, so I cannot confirm the build steps or dependencies. The README and homepage mention no accounts, hardware, or first-run configuration. The shell and the MIDI input setup are described only at a high level.
brief.standout: It is a self-contained SoundFont 2 synthesizer that is meant to be embedded as much as used. The homepage notes that several GUI frontends and music programs (QSynth, wxFluid, LMMS, MusE, Denemo and others) are built on its API, while FluidSynth itself has no GUI.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage news lists releases 2.5.5 (12 June 2026), 2.5.6 (4 July 2026), 2.5.7 (25 July 2026), 2.6.0 (11 August 2026) and 2.6.1 (19 September 2026). The homepage lists Tom Moebert as current maintainer. The GitHub README shows CI badges across Linux, FreeBSD, Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, Solaris and OS/2. I did not check commit dates.
brief.caveats: There is no GUI; users must use the command line shell, a frontend, or code against the API. The source is under the LGPL 2.1, and the README points to the wiki's LicensingFAQ for commercial or closed-source use. The scout note calls it fairly well known. The homepage's text is a nearly verbatim copy of the README's project description, so I found little that is new there.
quotes: FluidSynth is a cross-platform, real-time software synthesizer based on the Soundfont 2 specification.
FluidSynth itself does not have a graphical user interface, but due to its powerful API several applications utilize it
It is the software analogue of a MIDI synthesizer.
